statement: On newly published two-sided tablets whose one side reads 'N long strokes + G700' (or 'G700 + N'), tablets sharing the same text on the other side share the same N more often than chance.
basis: results/ration_chit_scouting.md (merged ICIT, 340 Harappa tablets: same-text pairs share N 50-59% vs 33% shuffled, p<=0.0002; holds for incised tablets alone, without the commonest text, and with each text capped at 4 tablets). All existing tablets have been seen.
data: Two-sided tablets absent from the merged ICIT corpus (e.g. future CISI volumes or HARP publications), transcribed in Wells/ICIT numbers.
statistic: share of same-text pairs with equal N; null = N shuffled among the new unit tablets (10,000x)
test: one-sided, alpha 0.05; evaluate only when at least 10 same-text pairs exist among new tablets
falsified_if: with 10 or more new same-text pairs, the same-N share is not above the shuffled share
